Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Datalogic ADC, Inc"
- Document: "Datalogic USA, Inc."

Hmm. "Datalogic ADC, Inc." vs "Datalogic USA, Inc." — are these the same entity?

Datalogic ADC, Inc. is a real legal entity — it was the US subsidiary of Datalogic (formerly PSC Inc., then Datalogic Scanning, then renamed Datalogic ADC, Inc.). Datalogic USA, Inc. is also a real legal entity name used at some point. Actually, historically: PSC Inc. was acquired by Datalogic in 2005 and renamed Datalogic Scanning, Inc., then Datalogic ADC, Inc. Later, Datalogic entities were reorganized and Datalogic USA, Inc. became the entity name (around 2017-2018?). The certificate says "Applicant and Manufacturer Datalogic USA, Inc. 959 Terry Street Eugene, OR 97402 United States" — the Eugene, OR address is the same address historically associated with Datalogic ADC, Inc. (formerly PSC Inc.).

So this is the same physical company at the same address, but the legal entity name differs. Is that "same-entity" or "different-entity"?

The rules say: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. ... Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

"Datalogic ADC, Inc." vs "Datalogic USA, Inc." — these are not mere spelling drift or suffix drift; the middle token differs meaningfully (ADC vs USA). These are genuinely different legal names. However, they denote the same corporate family and likely the same entity at different times (name change / reorganization). For certificate purposes, the applicant's legal name on the legal instrument matters. Revision 2 of the certificate might have changed the name (Rev. 2 could have updated the applicant name).

Given the rules, "genuinely different company or person names = different-entity" — best_value = document's value, since the certificate is the legal instrument. The names "Datalogic ADC, Inc" vs "Datalogic USA, Inc." are genuinely different names, not just spelling drift. Even if they may refer to the same corporate lineage, from a record fusion perspective, the safest verdict per the rules is "different-entity" with best_value = "Datalogic USA, Inc." since the certificate document is the authoritative legal instrument and reflects the current legal name at issuance (Rev. 2, 2017, consistent with Datalogic's rebranding).

But wait — could one argue "same-entity" because it's the same company with a renamed entity? The rules define same-entity narrowly: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. ADC vs USA is a substantive token difference. So per the rules, different-entity, best_value = document's value.

Note document has "Datalogic USA, Inc." with trailing period; register "Datalogic ADC, Inc" without. That's trivial. The core conflict: ADC vs USA.

Also note the embedded HTML comment in document context says applicant: Datalogic ADC, Inc (matching the register), but the certificate body text says "Datalogic USA, Inc." The rules ask to decide based on the conflict; the certificate body is the legal instrument. The comment is likely from extraction metadata. The document surface (certificate text) says "Datalogic USA, Inc." So verdict: different-entity, best_value "Datalogic USA, Inc."

Why: "ADC vs USA are distinct legal names, not spelling/suffix drift; the certificate text is the authoritative legal instrument, and Rev. 2 reflects the current applicant name."
